Cluster bootstrap literature supports resampling independent users with all their paired clean/corrupted observations intact; treating prefixes or corruption draws as independent users creates pseudoreplication. For this task, a defensible adaptation is to average paired differences within each user, resample users within category, then macro-average category effects. Multiple prefixes improve within-user measurement but do not increase the independent sample size. With only five users/category, bootstrap intervals remain exploratory: published work warns that few-cluster resampling can underestimate uncertainty. [ClusterBootstrap](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7148287/)

Separate uncertainty from user sampling and stochastic corruption. An adapted nested protocol uses outer user resampling and inner repeated corruption draws, retaining clean/corrupted pairing and shared random draws across compared conditions. Keep overlapping prefixes together; resample prefixes only when their sampling mechanism warrants it. Report conditional corruption Monte Carlo error separately from between-user uncertainty, and check interval stability as corruption repetitions increase. More repetitions reduce simulation noise, not uncertainty caused by having few users. [Monte Carlo error assessment](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3337209/)

For calibration, corruption benchmarks provide a precedent for controlled severity sweeps, while simulation-methodology guidance emphasizes known truth, coverage and Monte Carlo error. Adapt these ideas using zero-dose controls and predefined synthetic faults at increasing strengths; measure false alarms, detection power and response curves across repeated diagnostic samples. Test monotonicity rather than assuming it. Known injected severity alone does not establish a known diagnostic effect or validate confidence-interval coverage; those require a specified generating process or accurately estimated reference effect. These are proposed adaptations, not a validated recommendation-specific protocol. [Corruption benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.12261), [Simulation-study guidance](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8086)
